cohort: Patients aged 18-40 years who underwent TOLAC (n=57), normal vaginal delivery (n=72), or elective caesarean sections (n=60) at Ankara Koru Hospital between January 1, 2019, and January 1, 2022.
finding: While uterine rupture remains a key concern, the rate of successful vaginal birth after caesarean (VBAC) was high, suggesting TOLAC can be recommended to eligible patients in tertiary centers.
mod_finding: The study found that the rate of successful VBAC remained high, even when factors increasing its success were excluded, supporting the recommendation of TOLAC for eligible patients.
birth_weight: Measured and compared across groups; NVD group had statistically significantly lower birth weight.
gest_age: Measured and compared across groups; NVD group had statistically significantly lower gestational age.
